title: The Book I Was Definitely Going to Read
scene: You visit a bookshop with nothing particular in mind, resist buying a novel you genuinely want to read, then somehow leave with two discounted books you had never heard of before.
sceneJa: 特に買う本を決めず本屋へ行き、以前から気になっていた小説を自制して棚へ戻す。ところが帰り際に割引本へ寄り道し、結局それまで知らなかった本を2冊買って帰る。

chunks.ja: 買いかけたことのある

chunks.en: as if the story might have changed
chunks.ja: まるで物語が変わっているかもしれないかのように

chunks.en: I decided I should finally buy it,
chunks.ja: ついに買うべきだと決めました

chunks.en: partly because I genuinely wanted to read it
chunks.ja: 一つには本当に読みたかったからで

chunks.en: and partly because this had gone on long enough.
chunks.ja: もう一つには、この検討が十分長く続いていたからです
そこで思い出しました

chunks.en: that I already had several unread books
chunks.ja: すでに何冊もの未読本があることを
かなり辛抱強く待っている
その場で比べていました

chunks.en: the excitement of buying a new book
chunks.ja: 新しい本を買うワクワク感と

chunks.en: with the moral weight of the existing ones.
chunks.ja: すでに持っている本たちの道徳的な重圧を
思いのほか満足しました

chunks.en: I noticed a table of discounted books
chunks.ja: 割引本の並んだ台に気づき

chunks.en: and stopped for what I intended
chunks.ja: 立ち止まりました、私としては

chunks.en: to be a very brief look.
chunks.ja: ほんの少し見るだけのつもりで

chunks.en: I had never heard of before.
chunks.ja: それまで聞いたこともなかった
つまり良かった点としては
見事に我慢できたことです

chunks.en: I had actually planned to read.
chunks.ja: 実際に読むつもりだった
未読本の山は増えましたが
少し多様性が増しました

questions.question: Which boundary is most natural?
options: partly because I genuinely wanted to read it / and partly because this had gone on long enough
partly because I genuinely / wanted to read it and partly / because this had gone on long enough
partly because / I genuinely wanted / to read it and partly because this / had gone on long enough
questions.explanation: The two 'partly because' clauses form parallel reasons, so each reason works naturally as one thought unit.

questions.question: What does ‘what I intended to be a very brief look’ imply?
options: The speaker planned to look only briefly, but it lasted longer
The speaker had no intention of looking at the books
The speaker wanted to leave the shop immediately
questions.explanation: ‘Intended to be’ describes the original plan, while the next sentence shows that the brief look became ten minutes and two purchases.

questions.question: What is ironic about the ending?
options: The speaker bought the novel they had wanted for a long time
The speaker resisted the book they wanted, then bought two unfamiliar books instead
The speaker decided not to buy any books at all
questions.explanation: The self-control succeeds only in a very narrow sense: the planned purchase is avoided, but the unread pile still grows.

speak: Start casually, as if this is an ordinary visit with no plan. Give ‘partly because ... and partly because ...’ an even, balanced rhythm. Sound quietly pleased at ‘with my self-control,’ then let the irony build without exaggerating it. Finish ‘a little more variety’ in a calm, matter-of-fact tone.
review: Today’s flow is temptation → self-control → a new temptation → technically successful failure. Useful chunks are ‘partly because ... and partly because ...,’ ‘what I intended to be ...,’ and ‘resist doing ...’. The humour comes from defining success narrowly enough that buying two extra books can still count as restraint.
